english: How many cows did the old man leave? Ten cows and a hundred sheep. You are the elder: take for yourself those which you want. Let us two divide them in two. You will take the horses which you love. Who takes the old man's shield? Let it stay at the hearth for our sons. Now they remember him.
uncertain: h₁áyso / h₁áyeth₂er read as middle forms of h₁ay- 'take'; h₁áyeth₂er taken as 2sg subjunctive middle

english: Old man, the young man fell (sank). Why do you not weep? At night I wept. His fame is imperishable. What is fame, old man? Fame is the word which the grandsons hear. The body burns, the word does not burn. I still want that. Now be bold: that follows the bold. Are you bold? You are bold.
uncertain: final answer 'dʰr̥sús h₁ési' (2sg) to a 2sg question looks wrong: expected 'I am bold' or the question 'am I bold?'

english: What shall we give to father? His knife and his cup. He drank mead at the feasts from that cup. Shall we give him a spear too? We will not give him a spear. You will carry it. Let us dress him in the clothes which you wove. Dress him in those which I wove for him in summer. Will you haul the wood? I will haul it.
uncertain: usménh₁ / tóh₁ read as dual 'two garments'

english: Why do the women lament, grandmother? Little one, your grandfather (mother's father) died. Will he not come again? He will not come again. He went to the fathers and sits with them. What do the women sing? They sing his name. His name will be famous. I will also sing it. Child, sing, and he hears you.

Where did my (maternal) grandfather go? He went by the black path of the dead. Is the path long? It is long; one does not walk it together. The gods lead him. Will he be hungry on it? He will not be hungry on it. We gave him grain and meat. I will give him my foal. Child, keep your foal; he gave it to you.
uncertain: somHós ne stéygʰeti: 'no one walks it with another'?

english: How many kind guests will come to the feast? A hundred men and their women. Cook meat in the great cauldron. Shall I roast the meat of an ox? Roast it on the fire and put fat into the fire. What do we eat when grief holds us? The dead man eats with us and we live. Will you bring the mead? I will bring it.
